evidence: Clear module-based organization by domain (core, directives, parser, plugins, formatters, cli, utils) with bounded responsibilities
Plugins follow a common interface (Plugin base class) and are managed centrally via PluginsManager — typical modular monolith pattern
Core infrastructure (context, config, variable, regexp, etc.) is isolated and reused across modules without loose coupling
Parser and directives layers handle parsing and AST representation, indicating layered concerns within the monolith
Formatters are decoupled from analysis logic, supporting pluggable output formats without tight dependencies
CLI layer is separate but integrated into the same package, not externally exposed as services
No external communication or service boundaries (e.g., no RPC, messaging, REST interfaces); all components run in-process
risks: Tight coupling between parser, directives, and plugins may hinder independent evolution
Shared state in Context may become a bottleneck or source of bugs as modularity grows
Monolithic structure may reduce testability in isolation without careful separation
